data.answer: Restores are tested every quarter. The most recent restore test was on 12 September 2026 and was completed in 2 hours 40 minutes, within the 4-hour RTO, and the results were reviewed by the Engineering Manager and filed in the evidence folder.

Nimbus Labs uses 9 sub-processors that may process customer data, including AWS and an email delivery provider, and the current list is shared with customers on request. Customers receive 30 days' advance notice before a new sub-processor is added, and may object in writing within that period.
Tier 1 vendors are reviewed once a year, while Tier 2 vendors are reviewed every two years. Any vendor that suffers a security incident is reviewed immediately.
A background check covering identity, employment history and education is completed before the start date for every employee, intern and contractor.

The manager notifies HR on or before the last working day, and all access is revoked within 4 hours of the person's exit time. Shared secrets are rotated within 2 business days, and the company laptop is returned and wiped within 3 business days.

Customer data is stored in India by default in AWS Mumbai, but disaster recovery copies are held in Singapore. Because the disaster recovery replica is in Singapore, customers who need all copies of their data kept in India should discuss this with Nimbus Labs before signing.

When a breach involving customer data is confirmed, affected customers are notified within 72 hours, and Nimbus Labs reports to CERT-In within 6 hours of becoming aware of a reportable cyber incident.

The provided chunks detail severity levels and acknowledgment times (P1 within 15 minutes, P2 within 1 hour, P3 within 1 business day, P4 within 3 business days), a customer notification window of 72 hours for confirmed breaches, a CERT-In reporting window of 6 hours, an RPO of 1 hour, an RTO of 4 hours, and specific data retention periods ranging from the contract term plus 90 days to 7 years.
